name: Curtius rearrangement
outcome: Typically 55-90%; isocyanate, then amine or carbamate after trapping.
notes: Acyl azide rearrangement gives an isocyanate with loss of nitrogen; trapping controls the final product.

name: Baeyer-Villiger oxidation
outcome: Typically 60-95%; ester or lactone with migration-controlled regiochemistry.
notes: Peracid oxidation inserts oxygen next to the carbonyl; migratory aptitude controls regioselectivity.

name: Beckmann rearrangement
outcome: Typically 55-90%; amide or lactam from anti-group migration.
notes: The group anti to the oxime leaving group migrates to nitrogen to form an amide or lactam.

name: Hofmann rearrangement
outcome: Typically 60-90%; primary amine with one fewer carbon.
notes: A primary amide is converted to an amine containing one fewer carbon.

name: Claisen rearrangement
outcome: Typically 60-95%; gamma-delta unsaturated carbonyl with predictable bond connectivity.
notes: The concerted [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement is stereospecific and often benefits from a chair-like transition state.

name: Cope rearrangement
outcome: Equilibrium-controlled; useful yields when strain relief or product conjugation provides a driving force.
notes: This reversible [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement is stereospecific and strongly conformation-dependent.

name: Wolff rearrangement
conditions: ether or alcohol solvent, 0 C to reflux
outcome: Typically 50-90%; ketene trapped as an acid, ester or amide.
notes: Loss of nitrogen and 1,2-migration generate a ketene; the trapping solvent determines the isolated derivative.

name: Lossen rearrangement
outcome: Typically 50-85%; isocyanate, then amine or carbamate after trapping.
notes: Activation of the hydroxamate oxygen precedes migration to nitrogen and isocyanate formation.

name: Schmidt reaction of ketone
outcome: Typically 40-80%; amide or lactam with migration-controlled regiochemistry.
notes: Hydrazoic acid is highly toxic and explosive; hydrazoic-acid-free variants are preferred where possible.

name: Pinacol rearrangement
outcome: Typically 50-90%; ketone or aldehyde with migration-selected skeleton.
notes: Protonation, water loss and 1,2-migration occur; migratory aptitude and carbocation stability determine regioselectivity.

name: Benzilic acid rearrangement
notes: Hydroxide addition and aryl or alkyl migration convert the 1,2-dicarbonyl into an alpha-hydroxy acid.

name: Arndt-Eistert homologation
outcome: Typically 50-85%; carboxylic acid homologated by one carbon.
notes: Diazoketone formation and Wolff rearrangement give a ketene that water traps; diazomethane requires specialized controls.
